chunks: 2601 - It was narrated from Abu Basir, who said:
I heard Abu Ja'far عليه السلام say:

"Ali عليه السلام was with some of his children when Umar passed by him and said, 'What are these two dyed garments while you are in ihram?' So Ali عليه السلام said, 'We do not want anyone to teach us the sunnah. Indeed, these two garments were dyed with clay.'"

key_terms.أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ: Abu Ja'far, the Imam transmitting this report
key_terms.أَبِي بَصِيرٍ: Abu Basir, the narrator from whom this report is transmitted
key_terms.الثَّوْبَانِ الْمَصْبُوغَانِ: the two dyed garments being discussed
key_terms.بِالسُّنَّةِ: with the sunnah, meaning the normative prophetic tradition
key_terms.صُبِغَا بِطِينٍ: they were dyed with clay, indicating the nature of the coloring
key_terms.مُحْرِمٌ: a person in the state of ihram for hajj or 'umrah

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to wear garments dyed with clay while in the state of ihram?
ai.summary: This hadith relates an incident in which Imam Ali عليه السلام clarified that the garments he wore in the state of ihram were colored with clay, not with prohibited dye in the relevant sense. It reflects a jurisprudential ruling about what may be worn in ihram and also affirms the authoritative knowledge of the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام regarding the sunnah.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2601 - It was narrated from Abu Basir, who said:

"Imam Ali (as) was with some of his children when Umar passed by and said, 'What are these two dyed garments you are wearing while in the state of Ihram?'
Imam Ali (as) replied: 'We do not need anyone to teach us about the Sunnah. These two garments were dyed with clay.'"
